- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows steady, slow upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day), true outcome often overshoots — cap forecast slope at 0.3–0.5 per day after spike.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often over-anticipates — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (0.0) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for 2–3 days.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly downward and true outcome is rising sharply, model is lagging — adjust forecast upward by 1–3% per day for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and model forecast is rising slowly, model is under-reacting — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for next 2–3 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 100+ point spike), model often over-estimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and model forecast is rising, true outcome often lags — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days.
- If model forecast is rising faster than sentiment suggests, reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day to align with sentiment.
- If model forecast is rising slower than sentiment suggests, increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day to align with sentiment.
